source_evidence.anchor: Theorem 2.6.2 and its displayed two-sided tail bound
source_evidence.observation: For independent, mean-zero, sub-gaussian X_1,...,X_N and every t≥0, the theorem bounds P{|Σ_i X_i|≥t} by 2 exp(-c t²/(Σ_i ||X_i||_{ψ2}²)).
Sub-gaussian means satisfying the equivalent properties (i)--(iv) of Proposition 2.5.2, and ||X||_{ψ2}=inf{s>0:E exp(X²/s²)≤2}; the surrounding text declares C,c>0 to be absolute constants.
The tail, moment, squared-MGF, and Orlicz conditions are equivalent up to absolute factors; for mean-zero X they are also equivalent to E exp(λX)≤exp(K_5²λ²) for every real λ.

source_evidence.anchor: Proposition 2.6.1 and the paragraph introducing Theorem 2.6.2
source_evidence.observation: The sum of independent mean-zero sub-gaussians is sub-gaussian with squared ψ2 norm controlled by an absolute constant times Σ_i ||X_i||_{ψ2}², and (2.14) converts that fact into Theorem 2.6.2.

binders: An implicitly positive integer N and real-valued random variables X_1,...,X_N on a common probability space (Theorem 2.6.2, PDF p.18/printed p.29).
A real threshold t with t≥0 (Theorem 2.6.2, PDF p.18/printed p.29).
hypotheses: X_1,...,X_N are mutually independent (Theorem 2.6.2, PDF p.18/printed p.29).
Each X_i has mean zero, E[X_i]=0 (Theorem 2.6.2, PDF p.18/printed p.29).
Each X_i is sub-gaussian in the sense of Definition 2.5.6 (PDF p.16/printed p.27).
conclusions: P{|Σ_{i=1}^N X_i|≥t}≤2 exp(-c t²/(Σ_{i=1}^N ||X_i||_{ψ2}²)) for every t≥0, with c>0 an absolute constant (Theorem 2.6.2, PDF p.18/printed p.29; absolute-constant convention after (2.16), PDF p.16/printed p.27).
definitions_and_conventions: A sub-gaussian variable satisfies any, hence all, of Proposition 2.5.2(i)--(iv); for a mean-zero variable these are also equivalent to the linear-MGF condition (v) (PDF pp.13--15/printed pp.24--26).
The symbols C and c denote positive absolute constants, whose values may change between uses (text following (2.16), PDF p.16/printed p.27).
implicit_context: N is not separately quantified in the displayed prose, but X_1,...,X_N and the finite sum convention presuppose N≥1 (Theorem 2.6.2, PDF p.18/printed p.29).
Probability and expectation refer to a common ambient probability space, and the random variables are real-valued (Theorem 2.6.2 and Definition 2.5.6, PDF pp.16,18/printed pp.27,29).

details: The event contains the absolute value of the sum, so the estimate is two-sided rather than merely an upper-tail estimate (Theorem 2.6.2 display, PDF p.18/printed p.29).
The variance proxy is the sum of squared individual ψ2 norms, Σ_i ||X_i||_{ψ2}², not its square or the square of their sum (Theorem 2.6.2 display, PDF p.18/printed p.29).
The same absolute c applies uniformly in N, the distributions, and t (absolute-constant convention after (2.16), PDF p.16/printed p.27).

undebatable_constraints: Independence, zero means, and sub-gaussianity are all required hypotheses (Theorem 2.6.2, PDF p.18/printed p.29).
The estimate is asserted for every t≥0 and uses the two-sided event |Σ_i X_i|≥t (Theorem 2.6.2, PDF p.18/printed p.29).
The denominator is exactly Σ_i ||X_i||_{ψ2}², with prefactor 2 and an absolute positive constant c in the exponent (Theorem 2.6.2, PDF p.18/printed p.29).
The ψ2 norm must retain Definition 2.5.6's threshold 2 and squared ratio X²/s² (equation (2.13), PDF p.16/printed p.27).
No identical-distribution, boundedness, variance-normalization, or symmetry hypothesis appears (Theorem 2.6.2, PDF p.18/printed p.29).

ambiguities.issue: The theorem uses c without quantifying it locally or specifying a value.
ambiguities.evidence: The display contains c, while the surrounding sub-gaussian bounds state that C,c>0 are absolute constants (PDF p.16/printed p.27, after (2.16); Theorem 2.6.2 at PDF p.18/printed p.29).
ambiguities.impact: A formal contract should express existence of a universal positive constant, not treat c as arbitrary input or distribution-dependent data; no sharp numerical value is source-mandated.

ambiguities.issue: The displayed denominator can be zero when every X_i is almost surely zero.
ambiguities.evidence: Definition 2.5.6 makes ||·||_{ψ2} a norm, and Theorem 2.6.2 imposes no nondegeneracy hypothesis (PDF p.16/printed p.27; PDF p.18/printed p.29).
ambiguities.impact: The source does not state how literal division by zero is interpreted; a formalization must handle the degenerate case or specify an equivalent convention without silently excluding it.

ambiguities.issue: N is not explicitly quantified or declared positive.
ambiguities.evidence: Theorem 2.6.2 begins with X_1,...,X_N and uses a finite sum but gives no separate declaration of N (PDF p.18/printed p.29).
ambiguities.impact: The conventional reading is N≥1; an empty-family generalization is not explicitly sourced.

contracts.contract_plain_english: A finite independent family of centered real sub-gaussian variables has a two-sided sub-gaussian tail: the sum's squared scale is the sum of the variables' squared ψ2 norms, up to one universal absolute constant (Theorem 2.6.2, PDF p.18/printed p.29).

source_evidence.anchor: Theorem 2.6.3 and its displayed weighted two-sided tail bound
source_evidence.observation: For independent, mean-zero, sub-gaussian X_1,...,X_N, a=(a_1,...,a_N)∈R^N, every t≥0, and K=max_i ||X_i||_{ψ2}, the theorem bounds P{|Σ_i a_iX_i|≥t} by 2 exp(-c t²/(K²||a||_2²)).

The weighted result is introduced by replacing X_i with a_iX_i in the preceding general Hoeffding estimate, although the printed paragraph self-references Theorem 2.6.3 rather than the preceding Theorem 2.6.2.
The ψ2 quantity is defined by inf{s>0:E exp(X²/s²)≤2}, is called a norm, and the surrounding bounds use positive absolute constants C,c.

source_evidence.anchor: Proposition 2.5.2, especially the mean-zero MGF property (v)
source_evidence.observation: The defining sub-gaussian properties are equivalent up to absolute factors, and mean zero supplies the all-λ linear-MGF bound used in the Hoeffding argument.

binders: An implicitly positive integer N and real-valued random variables X_1,...,X_N on a common probability space (Theorem 2.6.3, PDF p.18/printed p.29).
A deterministic coefficient vector a=(a_1,...,a_N)∈R^N (Theorem 2.6.3, PDF p.18/printed p.29).
A real threshold t with t≥0 (Theorem 2.6.3, PDF p.18/printed p.29).
hypotheses: X_1,...,X_N are mutually independent (Theorem 2.6.3, PDF p.18/printed p.29).
Each X_i has mean zero, E[X_i]=0 (Theorem 2.6.3, PDF p.18/printed p.29).
Each X_i is sub-gaussian in the sense of Definition 2.5.6 (PDF p.16/printed p.27).
conclusions: With K=max_{1≤i≤N} ||X_i||_{ψ2}, P{|Σ_{i=1}^N a_iX_i|≥t}≤2 exp(-c t²/(K²||a||_2²)) for every t≥0, where c>0 is absolute (Theorem 2.6.3, PDF p.18/printed p.29; absolute-constant convention after (2.16), PDF p.16/printed p.27).
definitions_and_conventions: ||a||_2²=Σ_{i=1}^N a_i² under the standard Euclidean-norm notation used for a∈R^N (Theorem 2.6.3, PDF p.18/printed p.29).
The symbols C and c denote positive absolute constants (text following (2.16), PDF p.16/printed p.27).
implicit_context: N≥1 is implicit in X_1,...,X_N and max_i notation (Theorem 2.6.3, PDF p.18/printed p.29).
The coefficients are deterministic reals, while probability and expectation refer to the common ambient probability space of the X_i (Theorem 2.6.3, PDF p.18/printed p.29).

details: The absolute value makes the displayed estimate two-sided (Theorem 2.6.3 display, PDF p.18/printed p.29).
The denominator is K²||a||_2², where K is the maximum individual ψ2 norm (Theorem 2.6.3 display, PDF p.18/printed p.29).

The preceding derivation applies the unweighted theorem to a_iX_i; norm homogeneity gives ||a_iX_i||_{ψ2}=|a_i| ||X_i||_{ψ2}, and summing squares is bounded by K²||a||_2² (preceding paragraph and ψ2-norm convention, PDF pp.16,18/printed pp.27,29).
The same absolute c is independent of N, a, the distributions, and t (absolute-constant convention after (2.16), PDF p.16/printed p.27).

undebatable_constraints: The coefficient vector ranges over all of R^N; no sign, normalization, or nonzero condition is imposed on a (Theorem 2.6.3, PDF p.18/printed p.29).
Independence, zero means, and sub-gaussianity of all X_i are required (Theorem 2.6.3, PDF p.18/printed p.29).
The result holds for every t≥0 and uses the two-sided event |Σ_i a_iX_i|≥t (Theorem 2.6.3, PDF p.18/printed p.29).
The denominator is K²||a||_2² with K=max_i ||X_i||_{ψ2}; replacing K by another scale changes the stated contract (Theorem 2.6.3, PDF p.18/printed p.29).
The bound retains the prefactor 2 and an unspecified positive absolute constant c (Theorem 2.6.3, PDF p.18/printed p.29).

ambiguities.issue: The introductory paragraph says to apply Theorem 2.6.3 to a_iX_i, thereby self-referencing the theorem not yet stated.
ambiguities.evidence: The sentence immediately before Theorem 2.6.3 literally names Theorem 2.6.3, while Theorem 2.6.2 is the immediately preceding unweighted inequality (PDF p.18/printed p.29).
ambiguities.impact: This is evidently a cross-reference typo; the intended derivation invokes Theorem 2.6.2. It does not alter Theorem 2.6.3's displayed contract.

ambiguities.issue: The theorem uses c without local quantification or a numerical value.
ambiguities.evidence: The display contains c, while the preceding sub-gaussian convention identifies C,c>0 as absolute constants (PDF p.16/printed p.27 and PDF p.18/printed p.29).
ambiguities.impact: Formalization should capture existence of a universal positive constant, not an arbitrary or data-dependent c; no sharp value is required.

ambiguities.issue: K²||a||_2² can vanish when a=0 or all X_i have ψ2 norm zero.
ambiguities.evidence: Theorem 2.6.3 permits every a∈R^N and imposes no nondegeneracy hypothesis (PDF p.18/printed p.29).
ambiguities.impact: The source leaves literal division by zero unstated; a formal version must treat degenerate cases or adopt an equivalent convention without silently restricting a or the variables.

ambiguities.impact: The conventional source reading is N≥1; the empty-family case is not specified.

contracts.contract_plain_english: Every deterministic real linear combination of independent centered sub-gaussian variables has a two-sided sub-gaussian tail controlled by the largest individual ψ2 norm times the Euclidean norm of the coefficient vector (Theorem 2.6.3, PDF p.18/printed p.29).
